key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current govern molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These trends can guide parameter selection for welding low-thermal-expansion Invar components used in aerospace composite molds.
method: Evaluation of laser power, welding speed, and welding current.
evidence_signal: Across 5–6 kW, higher power increased penetration and keyhole size; across 0.5–0.8 m/min, higher speed reduced penetration and width; across 150–170 A, higher current widened the weld and improved arc stability.
watch_item: The abstract reports trends within limited parameter ranges but provides no quantitative simulation-validation errors or final joint-property results.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
